transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy. But I know they’ve been watching what I do and changing the pallet counts, trying to keep me from getting the supervisor position.
How long have you noticed these beliefs about your husband and coworkers watching you and changing the pallet counts?
About eight months, I think. That’s when I started noticing the voices too, and feeling like people were watching me or changing things around.
Over these past eight months, have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, stimulants, opioids, or other recreational drugs?
No, I haven’t been using drugs or alcohol.
During these past eight months, have you had any periods where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and felt like your thoughts were racing?
Some days I get really fired up, like nobody can slow me down. And then if my husband asks one little thing about the kids or my schedule, I just snap at him. It feels like he’s trying to control me.
During times when you're not feeling unusually energetic or irritable, do you still hear the voices or believe that people are watching and changing things?

Yeah. Even during a few quieter weeks, when I was sleeping more normally and not rushing around so much, I still heard the voice telling me to check things. I still felt like the pallet counts were being changed against me.

Over these past eight months, would you say the 'fired up' or irritable periods have been happening most of the time, or have they been more occasional compared to the weeks when you mainly just had the voices and the beliefs about being watched?
More than half the time, honestly. I’ve been getting fired up, barely sleeping, taking on too much, and then getting irritated if anybody tries to slow me down.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations commanding her to check things, delusions of persecution/reference involving coworkers and husband altering pallet counts) for approximately 8 months. Critically, she reports a period of mood symptoms consistent with mania (elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, increased energy/activity, racing thoughts, irritability) that co-occurred with psychotic symptoms and were present for the majority of the illness duration (>50% of the time), satisfying Criterion C for schizoaffective disorder. However, she also confirmed experiencing hallucinations and delusions during at least a 2-week period when mood symptoms were absent ('quieter weeks' with normal sleep and no rushing), satisfying Criterion B (psychotic symptoms without prominent mood symptoms for ≥2 weeks during the illness). Substance use and general medical causes were ruled out. The combination of concurrent mood and psychotic symptoms plus a documented period of psychosis without mood symptoms, in the context of manic-spectrum mood symptoms, supports Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type over Schizophrenia (which would not require the prominent mood component) or Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (which would not include psychosis outside mood episodes).
